posts.text: Medicare for All is the only health reform policy that truly fits on a bumper sticker. Incremental policies are inherently more complicated to explain. The ACA did much more than ban pre-existing condition exclusions, but that part was easy for people to grasp.

Medicare for All is the only health reform policy that truly fits on a bumper sticker. Incremental policies are inherently more complicated to explain. The ACA did much more than ban pre-existing condition exclusions, but that part was easy for people to grasp.

A story from our news operation about patients getting caught up in errors in Medicaid computer systems, operated by a private contractor. This is a symptom of a health insurance system that has become mind-numbingly complex.

I see lots of mentions of the cost of Medicare for All. But, it actually wouldn't necessarily increase health spending, and could actually decrease it. What it would do -- which would be controversial -- is redistribute health care spending from premiums and out-of-pocket costs to taxes.
